title: Introduce lint-telemetry sidecar and staged release-sync to reduce presubmit noise
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit runs surface a lot of noisy telemetry spikes and intermittent release webhook collisions that cause redundant release-signing attempts and flakey post-merge jobs. This PR separates telemetry collection from the lint runner (so lint failures are not held up by telemetry uploads) and adds a small staged release-sync service that serializes release signing windows to avoid duplicate pushes.

What I changed (high-level):
- Add a lightweight telemetry sidecar image + k8s job wrapper that collects lint telemetry asynchronously and batches uploads (infrastructure/ci/telemetry-sidecar).
- Replace in-run HTTP telemetry POSTs inside .github/workflows/lint.yml with an async enqueue to the sidecar via a local unix socket. The sidecar uploads with exponential backoff and retires without failing the presubmit.
- Introduce tools/release/syncer.py: a minimal lock-based release window coordinator (uses signed lease in dynamo/kv (mocked locally via sqlite for dev)). Releases now attempt to acquire a short lease before invoking the release-signer step. This prevents duplicate signer invocations in concurrent merge windows.
- Bump actions/checkout to v4 and node-setup to pin v16.20 in .github/workflows for consistency with our hermetic build images.
- Add docs: sdk/ci/README.md describing the new sidecar contract and local dev flow.
- Small build-tooling tidy: package.json devDeps pin (ci-related devtools) to reduce transient breakage.

Why this is different: Instead of trying to make the lint job more reliable by layering retries into each job, we decouple telemetry (best-effort) and treat release signing as a short-lived critical section. The goal is lower noise (fewer presubmit reruns caused by telemetry timeouts) and fewer duplicate release actions that require manual remediation.

Testing and rollout plan:
1) CI unit + integration: run lint workflow with sidecar stubbed (this PR).
2) Canary: enable sidecar for the infra-team repo first for 48h, observe telemetry backlog and retry profile.
3) Release-sync: enable lease acquisition for non-production release lanes first; monitor for blocked windows.
4) Full rollout once telemetry backlog < threshold and release collisions drop to 0 for canary period.

Linear references: ENG-4217 (telemetry reliability), ENG-4220 (release collisions).

Checklist: 
- [x] Add sidecar image and CI orchestration changes
- [x] Replace direct telemetry POSTs with enqueue path
- [x] Add release-syncer and tests
- [x] Update CI workflows and pin checkout/node versions
- [x] Docs updated

Notes for reviewers: The sidecar intentionally does not make presubmit jobs dependent on telemetry success — this is a behavioral change that reduces noise. The release-syncer is intentionally small and uses an injectable lease backend; for hosted we will swap the sqlite dev shim to the production kv-backed implementation in a follow-up (ENG-4230).
